title: Crisis text line triage and queue protocol: delivery, acceptance and time to first human reply
subtitle: Implementation study with RE-AIM outcomes and an interrupted time series of service measures
statement: Evening waits for a first human reply on the regional crisis text line have risen to a median of about 11 minutes and about 1 in 8 conversations end before anyone answers. A triage and queue protocol (automated first reply, keyword flagging of high-risk messages, surge roster) goes live for all shifts in January 2027. The evaluation will establish whether the protocol is delivered as intended, accepted by volunteers, and followed by shorter waits and fewer abandoned conversations.
whoAffected: People in crisis who text the line, many of them young or unable to speak safely by phone; volunteer responders and paid counsellors; the agency and the hospital psychiatry department.
whatHurts: A long wait at the moment of crisis can deepen distress or end contact; texters describe feeling ignored. Volunteers carry the pressure of a queue they cannot clear.
currentPractice: First-come first-served queue, no automated acknowledgement, two counsellors per shift for escalation, and no systematic monitoring of waits beyond monthly platform summaries.
whyNow: The protocol goes live on 11 January 2027, the ethics board has approved the evaluation on condition of a data-sharing agreement, and pre-implementation data exist only in the vendor's logs.
constraints: No funding beyond staff time. Evaluators may not read message content; only timestamps, queue data and the keyword flag may be used. The protocol goes live for all shifts in January 2027, so there is no concurrent comparison group. Research activities may take no more than 20 minutes of each volunteer's time.
patientCenteredGoal: Everyone who texts the line in crisis receives a human reply quickly, with the most urgent messages answered first, without anyone reading more of their words than their care requires.
summary: Problem framed as an implementation question about a service-wide protocol, with delivery, acceptance and service outcomes.
